Unity is essential in the face of disaster.

findings.name: Memo: A Disappointed Researcher
findings.text:
Truly, I never knew I would receive a warning from the highest levels of authority.

The rejection mail rejected more than just an application. It rejected years of my hard work. That's why it hurts. Yet, I believe my research thesis to be the correct one. The method for cultivating quality Originium lies within the data of that great conflict. I've studied every existing Originium cultivation approach, whether based on the compression theory or the activation theory... Because I know they all trace back to the same place, the same starting point: the First Aggeloi War.

I know you might be spouting things like "stop believing in folklore" when you reach this point. But I assure you, my thesis has nothing to do with "folklore". Our member most devoted to the field of history — may fortune shine upon him in everything he does — has gone to Wuling to further his studies.

The First Aggeloi War is inescapable for our research. It was ended by the Endministrator and forty other heroes. The most powerful forty individuals ... in terms of combat techniques and the Originium Arts. They were there from the beginning, fighting on the frontlines and witnessing the war's most intense engagements. This is why I must peruse their combat records. You may have rejected my previous application, but I shall persist and submit more.

And if all else fails, I will go north and join the Order of Steel Oath. At least then I could meet Castellan Zasso. He was one of the forty. He will have the answers I need.

findings.name: UWST Crew Discussions
findings.text:
I'm old. These flowers and plants are my only companion.
And I'm not that old anyway. I still got what it takes to fight the rock buggers.
And I've seen bigger Ankhors than those three. There's nothing to fear, children.

findings.name: A Complaint About Delivery Fees
findings.text:
500 T-Creds. Just for delivering a few notebooks to Morospolis?

What blightery is this? Are these notebooks getting delivered by the Endmin with the mighty Dijiang?

findings.name: Chat Records: Hikers
findings.text:
There are Landbreakers at the Science Park too. Fortunately, I saw the Collinses as well. They probably got the sitch under control.

Maybe we should meet up with them once we catch a breather.

I just sprained my ankle at the stairs after coming back! I DID NOT FALL OFF THE MOUNTAIN OR BREAK MY LEGS!

......

By Talos! What did you tell Rossi? I DID NOT kick the bejeepers out of 5 LBs, then crawled back to base on my own!

......

FINE...! That's what I did! Kicked the bejeepers out of 5 friggin' LBs, then crawled back to base with a bone sticking out of my leg!

findings.name: Memo: Originium Scientist
findings.text:
Dad, won't be home this week. Science Park is really busy with stuff lately.

We're trying to validate a new mode of activation. Maybe Valley IV is all we need to revive the Great Originium Oak.

If this works, you gotta tell Granny Jenner about it. Old lady really had it tough.

One more thing. Tell Mom to stop adding aggagrit powder to the soup. PUH-LEASE! Make sure you tell her, Dad!

findings.name: Memo: An Observer
findings.text:
Every time I see a soul brooding in despair — someone giving up on life or humanity itself — I would bring them here.

Two freshly roasted fillets and two bottles of drinks... Nothing about life is unsurmountable.

This was place covered in hills just over twenty years ago. We detonated the Great Originium Oak to destroy Astarron. This action of ours created the gash upon the land.

People talk about the Astarron with fear. I don't. The incident revealed the power of humanity to me.

Though I've spent years talking about this to countless individuals, only the Lupo girl who just arrived two days ago understood the gist. Now that one has a great future ahead of her.

findings.name: Chat Records: Showing Off
findings.text:
I'm going to Simonch. Need me to take anything along?

......

...I prolly don't have an answer to that... "Why Simonch?" ..."Oh, I just feel like going." That sounds pretty fake. Maybe I should come up with something poetic, an answer worthy of literature.

......

I can't answer that. It just felt that I'd be missing out something if I didn't visit the Mother... But how should I regard the trip to Simonch?

Should I call it a full cycle, or a conclusion of a journey?

......

No. Just thinking about it is making me afraid. I might start feeling that my life is already done.

findings.name: Memo: Celebrate the Reopening
findings.text:
Wow! More machines! And more seats! We even got two more auto-vendors...

This doesn't feel like the super cramped monitoring station anymore. Used to be a place where you can just turn around bump into someone by accident.

Alright, crew! Time to offer praises most high to our Closed for Expansion project. Then we should get together and figure out how to celebrate the reopening.

Should we celebrate this at the Mining Camp? Gotta let everyone know that our site wasn't abandoned. We were just closed for expansion...

findings.name: Memo: Painter
findings.text:
My head's hurting... I don't think I can draw this...

I can reference the photo and add a dash of imagination to paint the Great Originium Oak... But I can't... It always feels that I'm missing something...

I think it's called "epicness"...

Should've not brag about this from the beginning. A crowd-pleasing panoramic painting of the Great Originium Oak in three days? What was I thinking?

Ugh. Just do my best, I guess. I'll just end up scrubbing plates at the camp if I lose.

findings.name: Memo: Emergency
findings.text:
The Blight rupture happened during the Ankhorfall. Things are really desperate. We must assemble makeshift beds and stretchers quickly. Take apart anything we need to make that happen.

The mines weren't the only place affected. If the disaster went soft on us, we could mobilize our crew to support other areas.

findings.name: Memo: Container Crate Cleaner
findings.text:
I inspected this batch of containers... And their contents ... have been around for quite a while ... quite a long while, actually...

I even found tinned provisions for the troops fighting in the First Aggeloi War...

Seriously now, people.

I guess if I keep up with this container diving, I might find some kickass super weapon like a Pegasian Silverlance.

findings.name: Message: Worried Scientist
findings.text:
They told me I'm a conservative... Hurhur...

I know. A few of us have retained their wild ambitions.

The Great Oak of Valley IV had fallen for 20 years. Still, they insisted on building up the Valley and convert it into one of the biggest scientific bases of the world. They want to achieve greatness in Valley IV.

Is this a dream? Or a continuation of politics?

The naturally stable rift seems like a great, valuable thing. But the great Mother disagrees. The potential of Æther testing will not secure the future of Valley IV. Instead, it will only invite disaster.

What do you think, Crowe? Stand with me and keep the hot-blooded youths in check? Or would you rather stand with them and fan the flames?

findings.name: Memo: An Idler
findings.text:
...I heard them talk about some sort of "energy" and "tests".

Are they running experiments for applied Æther energy tech at the Test Site?

I don't really know the technical deets, but I got plenty of scientific ideas and fantasies.

Maybe a day will come when they come up with a new source of power. We can utilize this new energy to fly deep into space and reach faraway worlds.

Where should we go...? Big Gassy Talos is way too close... How about Terra...? I wanna take a look at where our ancestors came from.

findings.name: Researcher's Notes
findings.text:
...What about the indigenous lifeforms? Do we have any ruins, tombs, or fossils? Where are they?

Before humanity stepped through the gate, we all believed that Talos-II was the cradle of the human race. If so, our ancestors would definitely leave some form of evidence behind.

But we have too little data... I have reasons to suspect that someone is trying to hide something...

findings.name: Chat Log: Idle Recess Chatter
findings.text:
...I don't think we made any progress.

I thought so too, but ... I guess we should think positive. Using transmitters for Ætherside observations is definitely the right way to go.

But we're just a tiny research team operating out in the middle of nowhere. How do we build a transmitter? We don't even have the technical documents for that...

TGCC might have some. Don't tell me they lost the tech data during the First Aggeloi War...

findings.name: Bloodstained Emergency Order
findings.text:
Stone of Aburrey. Eye 2. Living water.

Seal everything in the vault. Protect it with your lives!

findings.name: Memo: Janitor
findings.text:
Ugh. I'll admit my mistake. Sorry for walking into the wrong area. I'll update my access card promptly next time.

I'm not going to excuse myself again by saying I was only recently assigned to this post. I know the Test Site has many floors above and below ground, and that every floor is clearly marked. I'll pay attention to the signs next time.

......

Yeah, I know. Some areas ain't safe. Barging in without protection might get me killed. Got it.

findings.name: Guarantee from a Builder
findings.text:
Construction progress is definitely okay. But I can't give you any promises about the noise.

We got scientists working pretty close to us. Are they complaining about the noise?

It's not everyday when the bigshots greenlit an expansion project for Valley IV. Don't worry. We'll do our best.

And I know I shouldn't be asking, but you talked to the people upstairs, right? About the thing you excavated from the Quarry? Is it really that valuable?

findings.name: Valley IV Documented
findings.text:
Recently, our correspondent conducted a tour of Valley IV that lies at the fringes of the Civilization Band. Numerous UWST crew mates and frontiersfolk were interviewed to better understand the food, accommodations, and medical amenities available in Valley IV. ...Many companies have resident liaisons and agents operating in the frontier. When a Blight disaster struck this region, most of them joined various forms of search and rescue operations. A company named Endfield Industries demonstrated their effectiveness in handling various disaster-related crises. A reliable source revealed that many field operators of Endfield are veteran combatants and elites of their field, making them incredibly skilled in handling the challenges posed by the extremely hazardous environments. To date (the time when this article is being written), this Endfield "troubleshooting" team has handled and mediated more than a dozen Blight-induced conflicts and emergencies for the residents of Valley IV. ...We can even say that Endfield played an instrumental role in ensuring regional stability as well as the efficiency of post-disaster rebuilding. — And this concludes our Valley IV report from our special correspondent.

(By Raquel Jones)

findings.name: Thurston's Field Notes: The Hub
findings.text:
Body discovered in temporary depot unit 002, Hub area of Valley IV. Positioned in a semi-seated posture. Clear slash wounds visible on thighs and wrists, with deeper stab wounds at the waist. The fatal injury is located at the neck. Preliminary assessment indicates death resulted from severe hemorrhage due to a severed carotid artery caused by a sharp weapon. The victim's protective gear remains largely intact, with all four wounds precisely targeting gaps in the armor.

Based on previously gathered intelligence regarding high-risk targets within the Bonekrusher Clan, the deceased is likely "Guillotine" Gabbi. His moniker stems from the terrifying power of his great axe, said to be capable of cleaving even armored vehicles... Which suggests his killer must possess considerable combat experience? The attacker, armed with a sharp weapon and remarkable agility, first inflicted a severe waist injury, crippling Gabbi's ability to wield his axe, then targeted the wrists to further neutralize his offensive capacity... Then finally striking the legs to eliminate any chance of escape.

But ... something doesn't quite add up.

If the attacker could precisely strike armor gaps, why not deliver a single, immediate killing blow to the throat? Why expend three additional strikes during high-speed combat?

One theory: the attacker may be a revenge-seeker. Someone intimately familiar with Gabbi's gear and fighting style, rather than a naturally superior combatant.

Gabbi served numerous leaders: assassination, kidnapping, robbery... He was likely employed by Nefarith long before she rose to prominence. The list of those holding grudges against him must be extensive.

findings.name: Thurston's Field Notes: Origin Lodespring
findings.text:
Body discovered at the Blightcliff Observation Post in Valley IV, positioned lying down. Aside from a deep laceration at the throat, no other fresh significant wounds were found. Presumed cause of death: cardiopulmonary failure due to excessive blood loss and suffocation.

Given the wound's location in a commonly fatal area, I initially suspected the victim was sniped by a crossbow from the front. However, the depth and width of the injury don't support this theory. Based on the width, it would have required a massive bolt, but even if removed afterward, it should have penetrated deeper rather than merely slicing the artery.

If the bolt had been fired from extreme range with depleted kinetic energy, hitting the throat accurately at that distance would be nearly impossible. Currently, the only weapon on-site capable of firing such a bolt appears to be the powerful crossbow beside the deceased.

I believe the more likely scenario is another: the victim used the arrowhead to inflict self-harm, then discarded it.

Cross-referencing image data and assessing the scene, it's speculated he may be "Bloodeye" Sazaro, an important clan cadre with many loyal followers. His adherents all carry black fowlbeast pendants as symbols.

But this means a combat-capable leader, for unknown reasons, chose suicide... All occurring during the Bonekrushers' invasion of Valley IV.

While I don't intend to sympathize with him, a perpetrator dying this way mid-harm is clearly not a common situation...

findings.name: Thurston's Field Notes: Aburrey Quarry
findings.text:
Body discovered in the depot area of Aburrey Quarry, Valley IV. Positioned semi-upright. Large electrical burn on the back, extensive bruising and apparent internal bleeding in the throat. Preliminary cause of death: cardiac arrest from electrocution.

Cross-referencing internal files confirms the victim is "Will-o-Wisp" Vichir, a pyromancer. Bonekrusher pyromancers are practically historic symbols. These guys can focus, raise a hand, and teleport through flames with ridiculous flexibility.

But here's the thing: Vichir died in the worst possible position ... trapped within a high voltage fence. I can almost picture agile Vichir blinking around while being systematically cornered...

Wait ... that's what doesn't add up.

Vichir only has throat bruising and back burns, no blunt or sharp weapon injuries. Why?

Did the attacker come unarmed?

Vichir and the attacker were both trapped by the high voltage fence. A situation equally bad for both, or worse for the attacker since Vichir had numbers on his side...

There's only one plausible scenario. A pyromancer trapped in close quarters would instinctively teleport immediately. The attacker anticipated this: striking Vichir's throat violently and fast, interrupting the transfer... Energy trapped inside his body explains the internal bleeding...

findings.name: Thurston's Field Notes: Power Plateau
findings.text:
Body discovered in the substation of Power Plateau, Valley IV. Positioned supine. Multiple wounds on wrists, back, left chest, neck, and face. Fatal injury located at the heart. Cause of death determined to be massive hemorrhage from cardiac puncture. Additionally, based on blood discoloration, the blade used appears to have been poisoned.

This has to be "Volcano" Chacha! A Landbreaker notorious enough that even people within the Civilization Band with little knowledge of clan divisions might have heard his name. Before Nefarith unified the Bonekrushers, his name was the face of the clan. More importantly, he was remarkably young. Rumors claimed he wasn't even thirty. Had Nefarith not emerged unexpectedly, he would likely have been the one to unite the Bonekrushers.

So who killed him? Nefarith? But she wouldn't need poison...

Crucially, the wounds on his back, left chest, and neck appear to have been repeatedly attacked before they could heal. Most of these injuries were concealed beneath armor, which are impossible to detect through combat observation alone.

Unless the assailant was already intimately familiar with "Volcano" Chacha.

findings.name: Memo: Secondhand Terminal
findings.text:
Crap, I don't know what to do with this waterwheel.

All those books at home were stored together with the family records. Even if it hasn't been over a hundred years, it must've been seventy or eighty at least.

All these years in the Stockade, each family has passed down their own skills, and they've dwindled more and more...

All that's been passed down in our family is some skill with electrical circuits. This waterwheel issue doesn't seem too related to that.

Who even remembers how to fix a waterwheel? He Lao, or someone else? Whose grandpa or uncle had that skill anyway?

findings.name: Sketcher's Communication Log
findings.text:
............

Worried Friend: Where did you go?

Sketcher: Don't worry, I'm at the Ecological Research Station with those students who grow vegetables and raise animals.

Worried Friend: ...Careful out there. Don't let those Cangzei pirates sneak upon you.

Sketcher: Last time you babysat me the whole trip in Wuling, I didn't even get to see Qingbo Stockade. Well, you're not stopping me this time.

Sketcher: My "Eight Scenes of Wuling" series has to include the great waterwheel of Qingbo Stockade. And it's not just the Stockade, I'll find a way to sneak into the "Exclusion Zone" too.

Worried Friend: Yeah, got it, got it. Just throw your life away, why don't you...

Worried Friend: How about this ... if I ever get a chance to learn Thunder Arts from the Tianshi Bureau, you can be my practice dummy. That'd be way more useful than you getting yourself killed out there one day.

findings.name: Livestock Student's Doubts
findings.text:
Tianshi: My burdenbeast was sick all day yesterday, had to send it back to Wuling City for treatment... Gotta check if it sneaked a bite of something while it was out grazing. Don't tell me it wandered over to that sewage irrigation test field again and got into trouble?

............

Breeding burdenbeast for disease resistance doesn't mean breeding more energetic ones!

Last time it was secretly licking Woolsey's back. The time before that it snatched Mr. Lightbulb's diary and chewed it up in the field...

If it weren't my thesis project, I'd seriously consider stewing it...

findings.name: Memo Records: A Historian
findings.text:
Quit gloating!

They only rejected my thesis proposal! I'm still going to graduate!

If I can be allowed to temporarily set aside the professor's lessons and solely focus on the rejected thesis, I still believe that it is a subject we should look into.

Think about the First Aggeloi War that took place nearly 150 years ago, the battle where the Endministrator and forty heroes went into the Aurora. What happened in there? Aren't you curious about that?

So stop calling me a conspiracy theorist. No official records have been released about the events behind the Aurora. And of the forty heroes who joined the Endmin, only a handful of names have been revealed to date... What about the rest? Did all of them die in the Aurora?

That can't be true but why would the Big Three choose to keep their identities a secret? For protection? Or to keep something secret and reduce the possibility for accidental leak of information?

Something definitely happened.

Something's hidden within our history. Aren't you curious about this?

Ugh... I was curious up until yesterday. I often brought up the topic with my fellow crew mates when I lived in Valley IV. They called me a conspiracy theorist and folklore lover... Unlettered fools! The lot of them!

Fine. I confess I am still rather curious about things, but ... the professor might be right.

No matter what the heroes chose to hide, they were great individuals who made great sacrifices. Revealing the secrets might bring about terrible suffering, and make a mockery of those who had given so much. It is something that I cannot do.

Maybe I should switch to another thesis topic. Perhaps I can write about the rise and fall of the Landbreakers.

Masked Rogue,

Hola!

It is only a part of my journey but it might be your first taste of high adventure.

You have seen Qingbo Stockade from my perspective. I pray you won't forgot that exciting trip we shared.

Your good companion.

Martina

findings.name: Memo: An Exhausted Tianshi
findings.text:
People, can you be more serious when filling out a repair request form?

This repair urgency level is way over the top. I thought the Reservoir Station was moments away from complete obliteration.

Guess what I found. Dripping noises in the vent shafts.

I got it fixed. This happens when the filter meshes are not cleaned for too long.

Gotta say this, though. Your shelves are non-compliant. If we need to run an emergency discharge, the entirety of the Reservoir Station will be soaked in water. Including all the supplies stacked on your shelves.

Remember that downpour five years ago? The one where the flood almost came up? Seriously, why are you so careless?

findings.name: Memo: Someone's Advice
findings.text:
I tried to persuade them. There's no pressing need to adopt such lighthearted designs for the core module.

Sure. Young people like cute things. It's something I can respect.

But picture this. If we were to miniaturize this set of equipment and use it for Blight elimination at the frontlines or some other places, do you know how it would look like?

Imagine. Fully armed and outfitted Yinglung soldiers with these green, beany things hopping and prancing around...

......

Don't call me an old dolt! We're less than five years apart!

findings.name: Test Log
findings.text:
Tide Flayer Test Run 13:

The test run results were less than ideal. Perhaps the compressive density of the Xiranite was off and needed adjustment. This run also took far longer than expected, and I'm running out of Xiranite from the last shipment. Things don't look good... I wonder if Chun He just got lucky with her applications.

......

Tide Flayer Test Run 17:

Another accident... We were so close. The structural integrity of the whip gave way before it could strike the Blight Core. Proper targeting could not be achieved Where did we go wrong? I would have found out if I hadn't been interrupted by the people from the Research Labs...

Oh well... Projects aren't completed in a single day. Fortunately, I have Chun He on the team. The lass is smart, gifted, and a hardworking learner. Even if I fail to complete the Tide Flayer project, she could succeed where I left off...

Oh dear, did I just lose faith in myself? This is ridiculous. We're so close to completing the Tide Flayer. I will see it completed!

......

Tide Flayer Test Run 20:

The Tide Flayer can now maintain its structural integrity in the Blight, even at high depth readings! A true breakthrough! Unfortunately, we're out of Xiranite. I don't know when the next test run can begin. Say... I wonder where Chun He has gone... I haven't seen the lass for a while... The weather's getting colder too...

......

Tide Flayer Test Run 22:

This is it! I've fallen short! Preposterous! Why did I spend so many years on this pursuit only to find this answer? Was it all for nothing? If the Tide Flayer couldn't locate the Blight Core, how could we ever hope to take out the Blight? This is utterly pathetic!

I see no point in continuing this project... It's over. This is where it ends. Chun He... that poor girl still has faith in me... but all I did was delay her entire career. She deserves far better. Speaking of which, when was the last time she returned to the lab...?

findings.name: Stele Inscriptions
findings.text:
The nation of Great Yan has gone to great measures to gather the knowledge contained within. This trove is invaluable.

If allowed to spread across the world, every individual will be able to emulate them and usher in an age of order and prosperity.

However, the Aggeloid invasion has laid waste to everything. Measures were taken to safeguard the gathered knowledge for the future.

Once the war ends and swords can be reforged into plowshares, solve these mechanisms and return the three lights to reveal the secret trove.

May our posterity witness our work, put it to good use, carry on our legacy, and live up to the dreams of this great enterprise.

findings.text:
Search results for: "Chi Xiao" (transl. Crimson Sky) (History Section)
----
Conquest by the Crimson Ameer (Sargon)

A popular Acahuallan epic about the conquests and territorial expansions of a Sargonian warlord named the "Crimson Ameer". His armies were known for their crimson-colored banners and brutal tactics. To this day, scholars still debate if this work is largely mythological or how much of it was actually based on historical facts.

Annals of the Empyrean Court, Scroll 7 (Yan)

A part of the secret histories recorded by the interior courts of Great Yan. The records specifically focus on major events of the Yanese imperial court and of various regions across a specified period during the reign of the True Lung. It is an important historical source for studying the shifts and changes of Yanese administration and government.

Fall of the Crimson Coats (Victoria)

A work of military history about the Crimson Guards, their annihilation during a succession war, and how they were eventually forgotten. It is a narrative of sorrow and betrayal.

Crimson Snow: Fall of the Old Houses (Ursus)

Written by a fugitive scholar from Ursus. The work analyzes how the old nobility of Ursus gradually lost their authority and influence during the unrest. The "Crimson Snow" in the title refers to fresh blood and hints at the melting away of old noble powers and privileges.

findings.name: Yinglung Duty Log
findings.text:
(Text transcriptions of an audio recording)

.......

Thank you, lady, but we cannot accept this. Also, this is a dangerous place. Please leave with the transport team.

Come now, kid. It's just a few packs of fillet cuts and vegetables. Look at you. All skin and bones. Take these and put on some weight already...

Lady, please. The Captain won't accept it either... Let's just ... ugh...

findings.name: Notes: Tianshi Disciple (1)
findings.text:
Data writing complete. I'll just submit them so my mentor and seniors can run the analysis.

Time is almost up. I gotta head back to camp and help my mentor bring up the measuring instruments.

Wait. What's on the other side of the bridge? Did something just roll across?

Is it an Aggelos? No way. This place shouldn't have an Aggeloid problem.

Looks like an Originium Slug. But are there slugs here? I think I heard my mentor talk about them on our way to Yinglung Pass...

I can barely remember the details. I shouldn't be revising my report during the ride.

I don't think my senior noticed the thing. Maybe I should remind him...

My senior gave it a kick. Maybe it's part of the experiment.

findings.name: Notes: Tianshi Disciple (2)
findings.text:
......

Nobody could tell that Yinglung Pass was just a piece of desolation ten years ago.

I remember those old photos I saw when I studied back at HQ. The place didn't even have living vegetation. Just dead, withered stuff.

Yinglung Pass is now a lush and verdant place. It's wonderful. In fact, I think the local scenery is on par with that of Wuling City.

But there's a tiny problem. The criss-crossing roads... I'm lost. It happened soon after I got separated from my mentor.

I should've left paper revisions for later instead of working on them along the way. I totally didn't notice my mentor leaving with the Yinglungs.

Well, since I'm here anyways, might as well focus on revising my paper.

findings.name: Notes: Tianshi Disciple (3)
findings.text:
......

The field survey has been completed. The following is an environmental assessment of the Yinglung Pass (YLP) area.

Levels of ambient Æther pollutants in YLP have significantly dropped compared to the data collected in Year 142. However, long-term ecological risks persist.

Several plants with strong pollution resistance have been identified in YLP. No significant contaminants have yet to be found in various water bodies.

Overall, YLP is currently undergoing a complicated state where natural remediation and persistent pollution occur simultaneously. We recommend applying strict restrictions for access and limiting various activities in the area.

REVIEW COMMENTS: Incredible. Truly. By this point of reading, I've counted ten flashy new terms. A full length paper of mine for HQ barely invents half as much.

RESPONSE: Of course, my mentor. I'll work on a revision.

REVIEW COMMENTS: This is the best written part of the paper. But it is also way off topic. DELETE IT.

findings.name: Idle Chatter: Yinglungs
findings.text:
(Text transcriptions of an audio recording)

Is this sky pole damaged? It's just darting about at random.

I don't think so. We actually supply the Oathkeepers with the same model. They're designed to be tough.

You know how to fix it? Alright. Give it a shot.

Wait. Do you really know how to fix this? Its lights just went out. Maybe we should... Oh. It's supposed to happen? Fine... Just carry on.

Oh yeah, great work, genius. It's not moving anymore. Can ... can we still save it?

WOW. You actually pulled it off, kid. Not bad. What did you do before joining the Yinglungs?

Wait. Do you smell something burning. Sheesh. There's smoke coming out of the sky pole.

Just stop trying already, kid. Fill out a repair application form. Get Wuling to send a proper technician here.

findings.name: Notes: A Certain Tianshi Disciple
findings.text:
Time really flies. Three years have passed since my mentor and I last visited Yinglung Pass.

During the last visit, I was just a freshman tasked with carrying the measuring instruments for my mentor.

Mister mentor would just reach for something. And I ... heheh ... just stood there. Awkward...

How was I supposed to know which instrument he wants. I did try a few times and got every one of them wrong. He sighed with frustration and helped himself instead.

Ugh. I don't know what I should focus on. I only got three days at this place. Will I get to find my research topic?

Why can't that freshman disciple stop staring at me? Yeah, well. Have fun looking troubled and confused. You don't know what's coming.

Blight my life! Even the Originium Slugs are making fun of me.

findings.text:
(Text transcriptions of an audio recording)

Day two at Yinglung Pass and you already found the audacity to come all the way here. Why don't you take a proper break?

Oho. What are you painting? Say, this brush looks pretty nice.

Did you buy this from some famous painter? I actually saw one wandering outside this place. Maybe it's that one...

You painted this? Do you know him? But isn't he...

Oh, okay. It's your younger brother. No wonder you came here all the way from HQ.

Yeah, I came looking for you because we read your file. It's your birthday today...

I'll tell them to cancel it.

findings.text:
I've infiltrated Yinglung Pass.

Yinglung Pass, a place of mystery, filled with the unknown, where danger lurks around every corner...

I've spent ages snooping around Wuling since I left La Fantoma, and I finally found my chance to slip in.

Gotta hand it to the Yinglungs. They got every place covered. But they did not expect a pro with diving gear.

That painter told me that diving wouldn't work and it was impossible to get in...

High risk, high returns. No one at the magazine office would dare fire me once I get a few amazing photos!

But the vibe's a little off for this place. I can't help but feel that someone's constantly looking at me.

Wait. There was an Yinglung here, did

findings.name: Memo: Tianshi
findings.text:
I just noticed. Is this an ink painting...?

Well, I can keep going, but... it's the bridge... it looks like it's made out of flowing ink.

And it's a long way down. Falling off is gonna...

Yeah. We did cross many bridges like this. But what if ... you know, there's a slim chance that... Look, I just graduated and I don't wanna...

Of course I know the Yinglungs have been using the bridge for ten years.

I just wish that I never knew that the bridges were just ink paintings. Now I can't stop thinking about that...

Sure, I know the proxy has given us permission to cross the bridge but... Look, I'm just friggin' scared...

findings.name: Comm Log: A Sentimental One
findings.text:
......

A21: Ten years. I'd almost forgotten what this place looks like. I could only remember that there used to be a bulletin board right against this wall.

A21: The team said we're taking a group photo after the testing. I even told my labmates to wear something nice. They replied by saying nobody has formal attire. So I suggested taking a photo at a nice place, then they made me choose.

A21: The bulletin board was the first thing that came to mind. It had good lighting and open spaces. A photographer would only need to work on the angles. And we could fit everybody in our huge team.

Stovemaster: Come on, Old Liu. Talk about sth else.

A21: But I gotta get it off my chest.

......

A21: There was this KABAM and I was the only one left alive. It ripped apart the entire place like paper. I'm decent with the Arts, so I quickly encrusted myself in stone, rammed my way out of the Labs, and rolled down the slope. I turned around and saw half of the team melting into the Blight. The notices posted on the board flew all over the place. One of them rested near my feet. I remember it being a power outage notification...

......

A21: That sight is terrible. I can hardly bring myself to eat ice cream ... or even see ice melting. So many died, and I can hardly recall their faces. But that notice ... I don't know why but I still remember it... It keeps showing up in my dreams, resting near my feet every time. And I still see every single word.

A21: "A 2-HOUR power outage has been scheduled for the Research Labs storage room for circuitry repairs." I don't know why, but these words haunted me for ten whole years. They've been burned into my memories.

A21: I never knew I could make it out.

Stovemaster: Me too. I only managed to bring a sapling with me back then. I planted it at the Reservoir Station. I thought it was my only way to remember my family for the rest of my life.

Stovemaster: We've returned. This time for real. You gotta look forward, Old Liu. Don't dwell in the past.

findings.name: IR: Founding of the City
findings.text:
......

In truth, the author once regarded "Suiming, a city in Hongshan" as a mere fictional invention when hearing it for the first time. However, after copious amounts of investigative work, the author found out that while "Suiming" may be fictional, written records and stories about the city were largely based on actual cities in various HAS Scientific Developmental Districts.

First-hand information gathered by the author via comparative field investigative work and site visits also revealed that many conflicting claims about Suiming are hidden within the scattered records. One of which would be the origins of the city's founding.

It is obvious that the founding of Suiming was based on the Wuling Science Station. Approval documents for building the site did not register it as a city-scaled habitat but as a small residential facility. However, both Suiming and Wuling Science Station were founded as facilities for Tianshi Pillar research.

Meanwhile, Wuling Science Station is situated at an isolated location close to the Wuling Very Large Rift (VLR), where Blight activities are frequent. The claim that "a Tianshi submitted a city-building application containing a report with extensive information gathered from multiple rounds of site surveillance" actually lacks sufficient data to back it up. The possibility that this claim is either a fabrication or is based on other HAS Scientific Developmental District cities cannot be ruled out.

Nevertheless, as a fictionalized creation primarily based on various facets of HAS Scientific Development District urban culture, "Suiming" offers a showcase of HAS focus on and vigilance against the increasingly frequent Blight incidents. This is highly congruent with their public attitudes and statements in various conventions and seminars. HAS has always held the belief that the Civilization Band cannot afford to be passive, and must actively seek countermeasures and solutions when combating the ever-present and numerous hazards of Talos-II such as rifts.

findings.name: Crew Mate Descriptions of the Illegal Photographer
findings.text:
UWST Crew Mate A:

...Looks like a woman. I don't know why she's taking photos of those things ... but it's super sus! Oh yeah, she was wearing this hat. And she's got some short, brown hair! That's right! Same color as my neighbor Lily!

UWST Crew Mate B:

I remember everything! She and I were the only two Felines at that time. I was carrying my toolkit and she was carrying a shoulder bag—Yeah! It's that flagship Brindle classic! Saw it on the ads! Oooh, I really want one too... Ahem. Yeah, went off topic there for a bit ... but I really want that Brindle bag ... it was a perfect match with her golden hair...

UWST Crew Mate C:

I was rushing back home so I wasn't paying much attention... But I think she's a girl. She was wearing this ordinary outfit so she looked pretty ordinary. I accidentally bumped into her and knocked the glasses off her face. I picked them up from the ground but it took a real while for her to take them off my hands. That's how bad her eyes are. What happened next? I went home. That's what.

findings.name: Letter from Valley IV
findings.text:
Brother, I think you should come work at Valley IV.

You keep thinking the place is out in the middle of nowhere, but that's exactly where it shines. Valley IV is safe. Neither the Aggeloi nor Landbreakers are interested in this stretch of frontier turf. There's also plenty of fun to be had at this place. I work at the Quarry and we got tons of events that include sommelier parties, body building competitions, barehanded rock climbing races, and mineral beauty pageants. And the best part is we're always coming up with more.

I'm learning barehanded rock climbing from this really old veteran. The geezer was part of the very first crew to start building UW sites in Valley IV. People say he was even a close friend of the legendary hero Aburrey... He's a master rock climber. In fact, he made climbing look like that Yan idiom: "Coasting along even ground."

Old man is really friendly and smiles at everyone. He taught me a lot of things.

Anyway, just get your sorry arse here. Together, our brotherhood shall achieve great glory.

findings.name: Torn Manuscript
findings.text:
...None of us wanted to shut down the Quarry. It's the very first large mining operation we planned and built in Valley IV. However, "depleted mineral veins" and "sub-standard mineral quality" are problems that the Quarry can't fix.

You know what I'm talking about, old friend.

The Aburrey Quarry is named after Master Aburrey... She's the legendary crew hero of the UW. You probably read about her story in museum exhibits or radio broadcasts, but I'm different.

When the Quarry was near completion, Master Aburrey scaled the peaks and blew herself up to create a rockslide. Her sacrifice blocked the Aggeloid host and bought everyone time. What do you think she was trying to protect?

Why did she push herself so hard? Is it because she cares about the factory buildings or the minerals beneath this place? You know she cared about none of that. She fought for the Valley folk, her friends, fellow crew mates, and children in her classroom.

Children, now that you're in my class, all of you and I should do our best to protect the achievements of Master Aburrey and keep danger at bay.

findings.name: Crew Mate's Fantasy
findings.text:
...I occasionally thought of the hills as barriers that kept things out, but they now resemble prison walls. The massive blocks of stone of this Quarry keep me trapped in this place.
And I feel like an Originium Slug or a strange critter crawling about the corner of this great prison —
I spend my day chipping and gnawing at the massive blocks of stone, and then... And then there is nothing much else to say, really.
I'll just chip and gnaw till all my teeth grind down to nothing. Then I'll keep chipping and gnawing till my bones grind down to dust. This is just a big ol' grinder.
Come to think of it, maybe it's a good thing that the Quarry is shutting down.

findings.name: Notes: Found From Somewhere
findings.text:
It was just an ordinary lab expansion. Nobody knew the results could be so serious. We just wanted a bigger sample storage room...

I don't know what happened to the crew mates who unearthed that thing. Hope they're doing well.

People call it the Stone of Aburrey in honor of Granny Aburrey. But you can't simply call that unknown entity as "Aburrey". That's so insensitive...

Will it trigger a violent explosion? Will it kill everyone in Valley IV?

But this might be another episode of my pessimism.

They stopped the digging when we unearthed the Stone of Aburrey. Who knows what's down there...? Maybe a Precursor data vault capable of propelling our science and tech to greater heights!

Ugh. Well, anyway, kinda feel bad about this, especially to Granny Penny. They fudged the numbers in the stone quality analysis report I submitted to her.

findings.name: Very Old Letter
findings.text:
I'm still willing to listen to those rather childish dreams of yours.

I'm still willing to sing those songs to the children.

I'm still willing to see you draw those worlds of fantasy.

I'm still willing to ignore those pranks you play on me.

I still regret not scaling that mountain with you.

"So many years had passed, darling. I can finally see you again, Aburrey."

findings.name: Memo: Piece of Advice
findings.text:
Ugh. If we gotta go, we gotta go.

A reassignment isn't a wildlands exile where we might starve to death. They're just shutting down the Quarry and moving us to another place to work. How serious can this get?

Speaking of the Quarry, just look at the yield and figures. Be honest with yourself. We aren't the role models of productivity.

A new job at the auto-farms or meat-packing plant would be great. At least we can still be useful.

Maybe they'll ship the entire crew to a brand new quarry. It might just happen.

You're grown-ups, so act like one. Changing places isn't going to make you a piece of deadweight.

findings.name: Will Left on a Trash Bin
findings.text:
I may not survive.

There are so many Aggeloi they've blotted out the sun. I don't wanna die, and definitely don't wanna die a coward. I'll probably volunteer for the frontline.

I got no family or friends. All my belongings are in my dorm room. Divvy them up, it's your call. My cred stash isn't very well hidden. Help me donate the entire sum to the children orphaned by this attack.

HAHA! The Endmin's here! I'm gonna live!

findings.name: Onboarding Essentials for Endfield Operators — Aggeloi
findings.text:
Q: I came from the heartlands of the Band and have never seen an Aggelos before. What are they?

A: Aggeloi (singular: Aggelos) are construct organisms comprising 2 parts: (i) the halo and (ii) the body. Their halos symbolize their "living" state, while their bodies are constructed by the Ankhor.

Q: People say Aggeloi aren't that scary. Is that true?

A: Absolutely not. Almost all Aggeloi have an active radius, and they will mercilessly attack any humans trespassing into this radius.

Q: Will it let me go if I beg for mercy?

A: Aggeloi have no feelings and therefore will not show mercy to any human.

Q: What should I do if I encounter an Aggelos?

A: If you are a non-combatant, please proceed to the nearest safe zone as quickly as you can. Simply put, the best advice is to: RUN LIKE HELL.

findings.name: Unrecorded Letter for the Family
findings.text:
Mom, Dad, you alright? I got an official job at the Valley IV site of Endfield Industries!

My colleagues are really cool and they take care of newbies like me. The canteen even served savory fillet on my first day and it's so yummy! But nobody wants to tell me about the source of the mystery meat. No idea why...

Almost forgot to mention this, but Valley IV is safe. SUPER SAFE. I don't think this place will ever get attacked by an Aggeloid host. Not in a hundred years.

In any case, I'm doing great and everything's good. No need to worry about me. I'll definitely make a name for myself here!

findings.name: Message

Take a swig if you're feeling flat. Go for it, people!

I heard Andre is slogging nearly 24 hours a day. We can't let him beat us!

findings.name: Memo: Siesta Taker

The 58th Worker Representatives' Congress of the UWST is about to start. I wonder if they'll say anything about Valley IV.

We got a partnership with Endfield and ran quite a few tests at the Power Plateau. Our achievements at Valley IV should be remarkable enough, right?

Sitch at Valley IV is looking up for us...

Maybe those on top might be impressed with our prospects, toss in some serious dough, and convert this place from a marginal production base into a scientific megalopolis. That would be super incredible.

findings.name: Memo: Hardware Store Owner

I'll then hand out the pneumatic drills, axes, and hard hats.

I don't know why my heart skipped a beat yesterday. Feels like a bad omen to me... Is something going to happen to this place...?

But where could I find these short cuts...? The Æther Test Site? That doesn't sound realistic at all...

Maybe I should try using the black grease...

The grease burns too poorly. The heat of combustion is way below that of Originium... The substance is hardly useful.
|-|
Page 2=
A few scientists came up with various theories about the black grease... "Fossil fuel" does sound like a fitting name. I guess I'll start using this name as well.

Some believe that such fuels also exist on Terra. The only reason we failed to find it there was Originium. The crystal "ate" it all up, supposedly.

I generated another hypothesis... Perhaps we had better fuels on Terra, but they were all "eaten up" by Originium.

Perhaps Talos-II offered a better chance. Maybe we can find better sources of fuel in this place.
|-|
Page 3=
If we fail to dig it out from the natural environment, or if such substance never existed ... we'll come up with something else.

We can utilize the Aggeloi... This actually sounds like a feasible plan.

Humanity has occasionally found materials with special properties from Aggeloid remains. Ankhors would forcibly gather and "mash" various bits of matter together in the process of Aggeloid formation, and give rise to these special materials at the same time — It's just like how the Yanese forged their superb alloys all those years ago.

But this requires better understanding of Ankhors... A field of expertise that I'm lacking in...

How would I design the three material input ports of a processing facility to achieve Ankhor-like production...?

I can start by sketching a blueprint...

What did those UWST slogans say again? Even a shop floor crew mate can do serious science!

findings.name: Records of Bonekrusher Atrocities
findings.text:
We conkered a outpost n' killed evry'wun who rezizted.

We grabd zos who did not reziz. Wheeled them to our turf to build the denstakk.

We shall cover the lands with our denstakks.

findings.name: Records of Great Ambition
findings.text:
One axe, two axes ... stuffed in the crates...

Get more axes and I'll be a Bonekrushing fist.

findings.name: Records of Zealous Joy
findings.text:
DEYS WEAK!

HAZEFYRE SHALL SKORCH DEYR THROTTS!

DEYR JAI-ENT GATES WILL NOT STOP US!

BAWWS IS SO SMART!

findings.name: Scribbles of Insanity
findings.text:
BAWS BLESSES! OUR FUU-CHUR IS GLOOORRRY!

ALL DEE-NAI-ERS AND WEAK TRASH ARE DED!

THEY DO NOT DESURV DA BLESSINS!

DO NOT BE A DEE-NAI-ER!

findings.name: Note Stuffed in A Wall Crack
findings.text:
Thank Talos they didn't find me. My Originium Arts helped me to "hide" in this complex array of colors.

To the one who find this note, I hope you can report the situation to the Security Bureau and find a way to inform the Endfielders at the Hub Base.

The one leading the Landbreakers is extremely dangerous. She wields a strange power. I have never seen Originium Arts of her sort.

A band of them probably used the underground tunnels to infiltrate the place and then opened the fortress gates. That woman ... she destroys everyone with a single move...

A huge flamethower brute knocked me off my legs. Almost smashed me into the wall, he did. Fortunately, the rest of them left me for dead...

No need to worry about me. I may be wounded, but I am still "fighting" them in my way.

findings.name: Notes of Insanity
findings.text:
THE BLESSING! IS! GLOOOORIUS!

EK-SAH-QTT ALL DEE-NAI-ERS!

POWER! VEN-JENCE! FU-CHURR! GLOOORY!

findings.name: Recently Posted Announcement
findings.text:
The 58th Worker Representatives' Congress of the UWST is about to start. The representatives of Valley IV will be heading to Mat' Gorodov, the "mother of cities".

Crew, I understand your excitement and happiness.

Nevertheless, PLEASE DO NOT try to shove supplies to the representatives as this would affect their itinerary.

Every representative's traveling plans and supplies have been arranged.

And please respect the break time of our representatives. PLEASE DO NOT visit the representatives to convey your feedback or suggestions.

Thank you!

findings.name: Draft of an Introduction
findings.text:
The representatives will be meeting at Simonch. I heard fellow crew mates from other production sites will be visiting Valley IV once the meeting is over.

They will be arriving at the Valley Pass first. Gotta come up with a proper introduction for this place...

"My fellow crew mates, welcome to Valley IV! We are now at the Valley Pass. It is the first stop for anyone entering the Valley..."

"It is an important supplies transfer hub for Valley IV..."

"Despite the rather small and basic facilities, we have a comprehensive fleet of self-service amenities along the pavement. These are more than capable of providing meals, repair toolkits, weapons, and gear for every traveler..."

Hmm. This intro is looking a little too long. Getting conflicted about this. Should I rewrite?

findings.name: Notes From a Crack in a Tire
findings.text:
My wound is healing... I think I can cast my Originium Arts properly again and hide my tracks.

If you find this note, this means you know me pretty well. In fact, you know where I like to play my pranks.

Help me call the Security Bureau or my superiors. Or go to the Hub Base and see if you can get in touch with Endfield.

The Landbreakers are dangerous! The Landbreakers are dangerous! The Landbreakers are dangerous!

I think their leader has mastered some Ætherside Arts!

If you're a Landbreaker...

I HOPE YOU CHOKE AND DIE IN YOUR SMELLY SMOG!

findings.name: Soth's Notes
findings.text:
Thank goodness the secret tunnel I used as a kid has not collapsed. The woosters are gone, so this is our temporary hideout. The tunnel leads to the substation and is just big enough to accommodate everyone.

I had to enforce rationing to make our supplies of food and water last as long as possible. Fortunately everyone is supportive of my decision.

But we can't stay here forever.

A kid managed to catch a long-ear and he's raising it as his pet. I hope we get rescued soon enough ... before we have to kill that poor little thing for food.

We noticed that people go missing during daily headcounts. I know they had no choice but to flee. I have no choice but to tell everyone not to lead the LBs to this place.

A few came back after a while with wild tubers, mushrooms, and seeds. It gave us a bit more food on the table, but many did not make it back to the tunnel shelter.

We're running out of food and meds... And the LBs are still prowling outside.

What will happen to us if we run out of everything? Is there anyone who can help us?

findings.name: Temporary Convention of the Shelter
findings.text:
1. Water, food, and other essentials must be distributed fairly (the sick and injured will be rationed separately). NO HOARDING IS ALLOWED.

2. VIOLENCE IS STRICTLY PROHIBITED. We shall enforce ZERO tolerance on theft, robbery, and fraud. All disagreements and conflicts shall be mediated by the entire shelter.

3. If you need to use wooster stuff, talk and register with Soth.

4. KEEP THE SHELTER CLEAN. All sicknesses and injuries must be reported.

5. Healthy adults MUST COMPLETE ASSIGNED JOBS before they can start working on other pursuits.

6. STAY ALERT. Do not venture outside. Do not reveal the whereabouts of the shelter. REPORT all unusual activities.

......

findings.name: Handwritten Memo
findings.text:
I wanna go home

I miss my desk and my chair, and my bed with soft sheets

But it turned into a wicked lair of prowling wildland beasts

I wanna go home

I miss the hot warm soup over some crimson stove fire

But a furnace now stood, roaring like a grim bloody howler

I wanna go home

I miss the golden sunshine and breeze of evening time

But it's now filled with scalding smoke and seizes up our throats

No one wants to go home

Because the place is no longer our own

findings.name: Ginny's Diary
findings.text:
■■/■■

I cant see the day or night but I think I lived in the cave for many days. My tummy hurts but I wont tell Karja cos I dun wanna give him no trouble. The pipey face baddy grabs naughty kids.

Karja spy-d on my diary and dun talk to me no more. I dont know where he went. Im gonna hide my diary at a super secret place so no one can find them.

I ran out of the colors but i remember where the flowers grows so i am not going to bother karja or Miss Arclight cos I can find them on my own and then draw very nice pictures of them!

findings.name: Celestial Observation Log (Valley IV)
findings.text:
(A stack of handwritten celestial observation logs kept by a UWST sentry. The word "Normal" has been written behind most of the log sheets.)

TIME OF RECORD: Observation cycle 1

OPTICAL EVENTS: None

SIGNAL EVENTS: None

EVENT DESCRIPTION:

All is well.

I'll be assigned to another department for the next cycle. Probably end up at the UWST Security Bureau. But I only just managed to set up the celestial monitoring framework here...

TO THE ONE TAKING OVER MY POST: I advise you to follow my format and template for making the celestial observation logs. It doesn't matter if you're a resident messenger, sentry, or crew mate. The primary responsibility of a celestial observer in the frontiers is to record special celestial phenomena, especially Ankhors flying overhead. You can ignore most non-essential data readings. This region covers 12 observation posts and you'll have to visit all of them. Work will be hard so you gotta conserve your brain juice for the most essential matters.

You have 2 units of Rhine Antenna. Keep 1 of those as your backup. We got optical lenses at every OP. Every post is stocked, but not abundantly so. Contact a nearby UWST or Endfield site if something comes up. Someone should be able to help.

DO NOT aggravate the local Aggeloi. The cleanup crew may have missed an Ankhor or two. Expect Aggeloid presence and KEEP YOUR DISTANCE.

Ankhors never strike the same place twice. That's how the saying goes. Your work might be easy.

Keep up the good work. Stay on target.

TIME OF RECORD: Observation cycle 2

OPTICAL EVENTS: None

SIGNAL EVENTS: None

EVENT DESCRIPTION:

All is well.

I'm a professional scout! I have started my celestial observer's job in Valley IV.

Let's do it!

TIME OF RECORD: Observation cycle 45

OPTICAL EVENTS: -

SIGNAL EVENTS: -

EVENT DESCRIPTION:

Normal.

TIME OF RECORD: Observation cycle 59

OPTICAL EVENTS: -

SIGNAL EVENTS: -

EVENT DESCRIPTION:

Normal.

TIME OF RECORD: Observation cycle 60

OPTICAL EVENTS: Drop in apparent magnitude of Talos.

SIGNAL EVENTS: -

EVENT DESCRIPTION:

The apparent magnitude of the system's star has not changed, but the apparent magnitude of the gas giant Talos has dropped by 0.27 during the evening, constituting a significant change exceeding seasonal expectations.

Maybe we should call this a random event. Correlating the brightness of celestial entities to Ankhorfall frequencies sounds like science fiction to me.

I've monitored 60 observation cycles and no new Ankhors appeared in this region.

It's so boring out here—

TIME OF RECORD: Observation cycle 61

OPTICAL EVENTS: -

SIGNAL EVENTS: -

EVENT DESCRIPTION:

See. Correlation does not imply causation.

TIME OF RECORD: Observation cycle 216

OPTICAL EVENTS: -

SIGNAL EVENTS: -

EVENT DESCRIPTION:

Normal.

findings.name: Memo Passed Between Cages
findings.text:
(A piece of paper filled with writing. It looks very worn and is probably passed around for a while.)

(Scribbles) The fort is finished. Gotta save our butts. Rest first and wait for the night.

(Powerful scratches) I got a knife. Pipefaces didn't find it.

(Scribbles) I saw the prankster kid before they locked me up. I think there's hope.

(Neat writings) They'll ship us out early. I'll try to slow them down. You should go ahead.

(Scribbles) We do it tonight. Got an alternative plan.

findings.name: Memo: Take Your Meds
findings.text:
This crate contains preventive suppressants. Give yourself one shot every week.

People still run the risk of contracting Oripathy when "kindling the furnace". Be careful.

findings.name: Work Records with Ugly Handwriting
findings.text:
The Originium of this "furnace" showed pretty impressive growth over the last 30 days.

When I planted the crystal seed, an excited scientist told me that the Originium can be harvested every 12 days with this cultivation method. IF the test results turn out great. This is just 2 days shorter than the original process, but I call it a good start.

Though we're not really low on Originium, we need BETTER Originium in the long run.

The scientist also told me that she's coming up with a highly efficient and automated Originium farm. Plant the seeds in the morning and you'll be harvesting the golden crystals by night.

I told her that she's dreaming. But then I dreamed of mountain-sized crystal clusters in the following night. Clusters that are even BIGGER than the Great Originium Oak I saw in the videos.

Alright then. I guess I'll work with her and turn this dream into reality.

findings.name: Landbreaker Note with Sketches
findings.text:
FIND THIS.

(A rough sketch of what appears to be a power facility.)

BREAK AND SMASH IT.

NO POWER FOR THAT VOUIVRE.

findings.name: Memo: Sincere Gratitude
findings.text:
Thank you, everyone, for your Originium samples! The large area Arts Unit is now small enough to fit on a lab bench! And that is AWESOME!

We got a weekend test scheduled at the repair platform. There'll be a party after a test. Be there or be square!

Food and refreshments available! PLUS a special performance by a mystery VIP!

I have a feeling this mystery VIP will be that "Tweety-Bomb". If you're attending, you better get suited up in decent PPE...

findings.name: Delivery Form
findings.text:
RECIPIENT: Yvonne

ORDER ID: ■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■ ■■ ■■■■■■■■■■■■■■

GOODS: 1L tub of nail varnish (powder, no UV required) + Blight-proof foundation + Transparent film (FREE)

NOTES: Got big horns.

findings.name: Celebration Notice
findings.text:
Originium cultivation efficiency is far below our ideal targets. Originium activity has also failed to reach satisfactory levels...

These issues have perplexed generations of scientists. I know we gotta rush things along, but things aren't that desperate yet.

Life goes on. People gotta eat.

That means: BBQ party at the canteen tonight. BE THERE.

findings.name: Handwritten Notes from Yvonne
findings.text:
You weren't around when I arrived. I placed a bottle of my special nail varnish blend on your table!

I saw your progress on the terminal. If you're stuck, try spamming the squat action at the left side. That should clip your character through the walls and escape.

Oh! Almost forgot the most important thing! I received the materials! The impact strength of this alloy is simply TERRIFIC!

YOU! MUST! NOTIFY ME when your department comes up with brand new materials!

findings.name: Discussions about Catastrophe Simulation
findings.text:
......

"Catastrophes" tend to occur in Originium-rich areas of Terra and trigger explosive growth in Originium clusters. Let's set aside the disastrous scenes wrought by the Catastrophes described in the literature that our ancestors wrote. Instead, we should solely focus on the "cluster growths" caused by the Catastrophes.

......

Active Originium clouds artificially created in cultivation shafts outside the Research Center are far smaller than their natural-occurring Terran counterparts. However, they still managed to reach our expectations for growth rates for future crystal cluster cultivation phases.

......

The crew mates call every test run as "kindling the furnace". A rather accurate description of the process, if you ask me.

findings.name: Memo: Cooling Facility Required
findings.text:
WWe need higher algorithmic capacities, and cooling facilities as well, naturally.

And we really can't simply lift an Originium formation weighing over 200,000 metric tons and jam it right in the middle of an unstable rift.

Our efforts in containing the Æther rupture still have a long way to go.

But there's already a flicker of light in the great distance.

Be optimistic, my fellow crew mates. If our research project continues, we're looking at total elimination of the Blight from Talos-II. And it'll take place in the not-so-distant future.

Yvonne is also borrowing my algorithmic facilities. Maybe we can ask Endfield to chip in for the budget? (Just kidding. Don't go and ask them.)

findings.name: Investigation the Potential Use of Grafting to Revive the Great Originium Oak
findings.text:
Let's skip to conclusions. All attempts to cultivate the Great Originium Oak in Valley IV essentially focus on Originium activation. Of course, this activation does not refer to breaking the Origocrust to trigger "bursts" of active Originium dust. Instead, it's an attempt to restore its original levels of activity — And by this I mean Terra-levels of activity.

......

This means we must attempt to answer that question: What actually happened to Originium? Despite spending years on this, we have yet to acquire a proper answer. Since this is the case, we might as well go around it.

......

A key issue is that we do not know when the Endministrator will awaken...

......

My plan does have its issues. Finding formations of high quality Originium and assembling them into a great oak does sound like a crazy idea to me.

findings.name: Memo: I've Seen the Light
findings.text:
My cousin has a job at the Worker Dorms. He heard the Endfielders talking about the Endministrator's upcoming visit to Valley IV.

FRIENDS! The Endmin is coming to Valley IV!

I have a feeling that the dean already sent out an invitation to the Endmin to visit our site!

Haha! We're talking about the legend who planted the Great Originium Oak! Talking to the hero will definitely give me a load of inspirations for Originium farming!

findings.name: Lovely Handwriting
findings.text: Feeling hopeless? Try escaping the other way...

findings.name: Casual Notes from Yvonne
findings.text:
After multiple rounds of comparisons, La Fantoma still makes the best coating. But they're SUPER EX! OVERPRICED!

NOTE: Ask HR to pay my wages in advance. Failing that, borrow from Andre!

Hmm. If I use it on my baby bot, maybe I can write it off as a research-related expenditure. This warrants some serious investigation.

findings.name: Notes Casually Written by Yvonne
findings.text:
■■/■■

The Blight simulation curve looks a little off. Am I seeing things?

WHY DID I NOT TAKE A PHOTO YESTERDAY! WHYY! AAARGH! I HATE MYSELF!!!

I'll run another test! And this time, I'll stay up all night and stare at it!

findings.name: Shared Musings of a Dream
findings.text:
I had a dream. A vision of a blood red river splitting open a mountain.

Astarron is immersed in this river. It has returned. I gazed upon it. Despair was the only thing I felt.

I thus turned around and ran downstream, down to the ruins of the Oak. The great tree burned, and the fire consumed me, Astarron, and everything else.

Is my dream coming true?

What should we do?

findings.name: Memo: Extremely Emotional
findings.text:
We'll just detonate the Great Originium Oak! ONE MORE TIME!

We still have the Oak stump at the Cradle of the Ages. If we find a way to rig it for detonation, we'll send every pipeface and buggerloid around it to Talos!

But how do we get past the shockwaves...?

Can we try using the Originium Arts? We can throw the demolition crew and charges over.

Situation at the camp is not that bad. This extreme option doesn't seem that necessary anymore.

findings.name: Memo: Mountaineer
findings.text:
I pushed all the ladders off and left myself 2 days' worth of food and water.

We don't have enough people in the camp. Nobody knows when the blighted shockwaves would stop. And nobody knows if more pipefaces would charge into this place if the shockwaves do stop.

We need more intel.

I shall use the mountain trails to observe the situation from various locations.

Buggerloids! Never underestimate human endurance and strength!

findings.name: Memo: Miner
findings.text:
The wind here reminds me of my farming days back in Hongshan.

I probably farm for my entire life if not for settling down the kid's mama.

I like farming.

Look at all these Originium formations in the valley. I planted them all.

Overall activity isn't as good as the wild clusters that can be harvested once every three months. However, the Science Park variety developed by the young eggheads grows fast and can be harvested once every two weeks.

They're just not that useful.

I really wanna see the Originium that my great-great-grandfather used. Were they really that scary?

findings.name: Warning from a Guard
findings.text:
Don't let me catch anyone trying to bike jump these cliffs! AGAIN!

Young and daring, eh? I'll hang you out to dry from a crane arm. A healthy serving of valley wind will cool you down!

findings.name: Diary: Originium Power Plant Worker
findings.text:
...What about the Landbreakers? What do they believe in? How did they grow up to become these raiders?

My Mother does not speak. Silently she consumes Originium to raise us. Her lifeblood courses throughout the Valley. She nourishes us so that we may excavate the flesh and blood of mineral ore, cast and forge bones of steel, and fill our souls with courage and a desire to build a better future. Our Mother taught us to swing our fists at the unforgiving frontiers and carve our names upon the lands of darkness.

But what about the Landbreakers?

Who is their Mother? Is she the shattered wildlands filled with nothing but suffering?

Or are the LBs our long-lost siblings who have strayed from our Mother?

findings.name: Memo: Wrinkled and Wet
findings.text:
I REPEAT.

NO RAISING ORIGINIUM SLUGS HERE!

findings.name: Old Reminder: Get Your Injections
findings.text:
Power consumption recently spiked at the Quarry. Got no idea why. Stay on target, crew.

This is also the time when I must remind everyone to keep Oripathy at bay. Get those shots or you'll become so crystalline you can't even roll yourself out of bed.

findings.name: Call for Recipes
findings.text:
Given the sudden nature of this Blight rupture event, we are now trapped at this location with limited resources. If you have any wilderness survival tips (especially about the gathering and processing of wild animals, plants, and even insects), please don't hesitate to share them with us.

Disasters may strike at unexpected moments, but they will never beat us to the ground.

findings.name: Memo: From a Crew Mate
findings.text:
Did any crew mate see my design draft? It should be somewhere at the corner of the wall... And I spent a really long time on it.

I would perform stringent scientific calculations when I'm not too busy feeding the boilers. Losing the data would be a real shame.

findings.name: Message: Clean and Simple
findings.text: This place has been breached. Apologies.

findings.text:

It shall be remembered, and be made whole.
|-|

It shall be engraved, and be made whole.

findings.name: Maniacal Writings
findings.text: BAWS, BLESSING, FUTURE, EXPLAWSHUN, DEEMOLISH, KILL, FUTURE, GLORY, BLESSED, IMMOR-TA-LE-TEEEE

findings.name: Researcher's Notes
findings.text:
■■■/■■■

The Stone of Aburrey was dug up at the Quarry.

■■■/■■■

The test failed. Perhaps it was a verification or interfacing issue. Maybe we can try a different approach by tweaking the currents.

■■■/■■■

That thing has Æther-related properties. It might be a way for us to glimpse at the Æther itself.

■■■/■■■

The only safe and stable tests we can perform in Valley IV ... are Ætherside observations and attempts to acquire images that can prove our work.

But this alone was a great bottleneck for everyone. We couldn't even figure out the most fundamental and basic approach to take.

■■■/■■■

I still have faith that humanity shall slowly pick itself up from the painful devastation. We shall no longer find ourselves wanting, and we shall no longer fear this world.

We shall get back on our feet, and look at it straight in the eyes.

findings.name: Letter: A Hopeless Soul
findings.text:
During the last couple of days, many friends asked why I looked so terrible, and how I got these dark circles around my eyes... I thought about it and believe it was not a big deal. I guess it's that beaker I broke. If we really need the details, I'd blame the beaker I tossed in the trash.

I couldn't stand the beaker. It kept asking me questions, so I smashed it.

It kept asking me how long. How long would these days last?

I looked at that rift, and saw ... nothing...

How long must we languish in this terrible fog?

My gramps told my dad that once we breach the rock stratum, we'd excavate even more ores. The wealth would eventually help us build a paradise at this very place.

My dad told me to get the science done and make Originium technology better for our civilization. The knowledge we gain would eventually help us build a paradise at this very place.

However, father...

The skies. They are gray.

The sky is gray.

findings.name: Corrections for the Rest Area Reading Materials
findings.text:
Fellow crew mates, I recently found several issues regarding the rest area reading titled The Warrior and the Forty Companions. I've listed them here for discussion.

First, while the publication is designated as leisure reading, I believe this genre must still adhere to the standards of logic and factual accuracy.

Everything about this book, from it's title to it's contents is clearly a fictional retelling of the historic event where the Endministrator and the forty heroes ended the First Aggeloi War. Given the somber nature of that event, the content should demonstrate proper respect for the truth — Unfortunately, the author obviously approached the subject with impropriety.

......

Fruthermore, the author also made conspicuous yet unfounded guesses on the heroes' identities. Not all of the heroes have been officially revealed. That is common knowledge. Ordinary folks might speculate, but this author presents these conjectures with a tone of absolute certainty that is unsubstantiated and troubling.

......

The quality of the paper is also abysmal and the text riddled with typographical errors. There is no question that the book is an illegal publication. I suspect the Sandreavers. Those Landbreakers wrote this to vilify our heroes.

findings.name: UWST Assembly Budget Proposal Briefing Draft (Version 8)
findings.text:
...Times are now different. Breakthroughs in material science and anti-Blight interference technology achieved by Civilization Band scientists during the last decade mean that scanning, containing, and eliminating Blight masses in the field is no longer science fiction.

We are now capable of locating a Blight patch's "origin of contact" and neutralizing it like untangling a ball of yarn. Although the exact form of the Blight scanner platform as well as the deployment and applicable scenarios thereof have yet to be determined, any technology that enables immediate, on-site control of the Blight is highly promising. It is a goal worth realizing.

findings.name: New Meeting Recap (51)
findings.text:
We now have 2 design proposals for the Blight scanning platform prototype:

PROPOSAL 1: Load the scanner on a heavy platform on par with a nomadic city plate, and start scanning and clearing out Blight zones one region at a time.

PROPOSAL 2: Miniaturize the scanner and mount it on a wheeled mobility chassis.

If it's the latter, a single field team would be enough to carry out missions deep inside the Blight zone. Yvonne's idea is solid, but I have a few concerns: miniaturization would mean sacrificing a number of functions, leaving the rest to be handled manually. Also, shrinking the prototype down to fit a wheeled platform won't be easy. I'm worried the objective might be overly ambitious and hard to pull off.

PS: But Yvonne drew up the blueprints anyway. See the attached files. PLEASE DON'T LOSE THEM!

findings.name: Opened Letter
findings.text:
The prototype is nearly complete, but Yvonne insists on adding a custom support AI and a facial expression interface to it.

She's clearly getting way too invested. I asked Yvonne if she planned to name the prototype — turns out she already did! TA-TA. What is that even supposed to mean...?

Let's hope she didn't just smash the keyboard to get that name. Anyway, the parts you requested are here. Don't forget to pick them up.

PS: The port parameters are in the attachment. PLEASE DON'T LOSE THEM!

(Flamboyant handwriting) The full name of TA-TA is Trans-Æther Tranquilizer-Automata. MEMORIZE IT!

findings.name: Tastes of V4: Workers' Borscht
findings.text:
......

Place the Originium slugs in water to make shelling them easier. Stew the deshelled slugs and burdo-fillet in a pot, then add some tartpepper and reed rye. Once the flavors have blended sufficiently, add crushed aggagrit.

NOTE: Many youths refused to eat the borscht after learning it contains slugs in addition to burdo-fillet (though the dish was extremely popular during the pioneering days of Valley IV). I improved the recipe by replacing Originium slugs with canned food from Endfield.

......

findings.name: Bounties from the Aggeloi (Issue 15)
findings.text:
Greetings. Pleased to meet everyone again. I got a bright new idea for Aggeloid Bounties — This time, we won't be turning them into condiments and spice. Instead, we're making a pot out of them!

Like before, we first take a larger piece of rock from Aggelos remains. With a chalk, draw the outline of a pot and use an Originium saw to cut along the line. Don't worry about making scratches on Aggeloid rocks as some of them can be hard enough to break your Originium saw. And there you have it! An Aggeloid pot!

There's the bright idea for today. Enjoy a culinary experience like never before. Remember, a good idea can even turn the Aggeloi into materials for rebuilding Valley IV.

findings.name: Memoirs: A Peddler
findings.text:
......

When I first arrived, I literally sold out my stock whenever I open shop. Choosing to do business in Valley IV seemed like the right choice at that time!

Buyers from the TGCC often praised my gear for sturdiness and durability. And thank Talos for the mercenaries of Seš'qa (if I ever run into them again, I better give them my most sincere token of appreciation). If they didn't help me carry the cargo crates, I'd probably get stuck at Valley Fort not knowing what to do.

So, having witnessed the prosperity shortly after arriving, I decided to set up a permanent place in Valley IV and apply for a branch at the Origin Lodespring. The crew mates complained that my shop is too far away from their place and the getting back and forth can be quite a hassle.

findings.name: Old Pamphlet: Recycling Tips
findings.text:
(Issue 3)

......

Still worried about the loss of the Great Originium Oak? Vexed about the ever-dwindling rations? Have no fear! We got some easy tips for recycling and reusing the trash:

Place blocks of ice created using Originium Arts in Originium fridges to reduce energy use and make your Originium appliances last longer without repairs.

When cooking rice, put fowlbeast eggs on the top layer of the cooker to steam them. This saves you fuel, time, and resources.

......

findings.name: Recycling Guide
Reeves Weekly Bander News Section
findings.text:
......
After the Blight eruption disaster in Valley IV, most supplies were delivered by the relevant staff to the doorsteps of the workers' registered addresses. However, many of the locals are still actively foraging for food from the outdoors. Reliable sources revealed that a UWST crew mate named Roman started making flame-roasted Originium slugs at the Valley Pass and offered them, free of charge, to a local temporary shelter that ran low on food. Having heard of this, our correspondent went straight to the site and tried one of the very rustic-looking slug kebab. It turned out to be quite palatable with a soft juicy texture that melts in one's mouth.

......
The Valley IV crew mates are working closely together and helping each other out. There is no question that the Valley will endure these trying times, just as it did twenty years ago.

findings.name: V4 Worker's Guide: Aburrey Quarry
findings.text:
...Following the detonation of the Great Originium Oak, many UWST crew mates went to work at Aburrey Quarry. Many mining drills broke down due to overuse. To cater to requests from the UWST, the TGCC will be supplying the Sandbeast Originium Mining Drill that features a coolant-based heat radiator...

NOTE: The introduction of the new mining drills led to a temporary spike in productivity. However, this is quickly followed by frequent breakdowns of the new drills. An investigation revealed that supporting crew mates from other regions decided to save time acquiring coolants by filling up the radiator with recycled sprinkling water from dust control. A number of crew mates also dumped seasoning and crudely deshelled Originium slugs (often found near the Quarry) into the radiator tank for cooking. Such actions led to reduced cooling performance of the mining drills. SPECIAL NOTE: The Aburrey Quarry has enacted a rule forbidding crew mates from bringing food into the Quarry Site.
