findings.name: Bureau of Swordmancers
findings.text:
The Bureau of Swordmancers (also known as Hongshan Swordmancers or HS.Swords) is an important research and production institution directly managed by the Hongshan Academy of Sciences (HAS). The Bureau is responsible for the research, development, and production of high-quality light and heavy equipment and weaponry for HAS and the entirety of the Civilization Band. While managing production at various regional branches under HAS, the Bureau is also in charge of auditing and distributing production blueprints, as well as conducting final quality verification and validation of the equipment it produces.

The Bureau of Swordmancers was founded to address humanity's severe disadvantage during the First Aggeloi War after losing the Cosmic Gate of Talos-II. The Bureau then focused its research efforts on developing weapons and equipment that can effectively counter the Aggeloid threat. This laid the foundation upon which the Bureau produced equipment with a wide range of specifications capable of fulfilling the needs of military personnel from various Terran nations. To this day, many pieces of old equipment manufactured during the War still bear these inscriptions: Manufactured by the Bureau of Swordmancers.

Even now, weapons and equipment manufactured by the Bureau of Swordmancers remain the first choice of HAS personnel. Products of the Bureau are still very well received by the market of the Civilization Band.

findings.name: Cabal of Tranquility
findings.text:
The Cabal of Tranquility is a technocratic organization that inherited aspects of the Lateran faith. Its current headquarters is the Monasterium, a nomadic city.

For more than a century, Cabal clerics have devoted themselves to restoring Terran technologies lost during the First Aggeloi War, excavating various locations of Talos-II in search of Precursor ruins, and providing spiritual guidance to the people. The Cabal of Tranquility has accumulated a vast number of technological patents approved by the Band Accord. However, the Cabal has made most of its technological endeavors free for public use within the Civilization Band, and only collects royalties on a small fraction of its patents to cover operational expenses.

Internally, Cabal clerics have organized themselves into three branches following the teachings of their Lateran faith:

The first is the Sessionites, whose clerics restored the Terran technology of Originium-based micro-electronics from the ruins of the First Aggeloi War. Their efforts helped the signatories of the Band Accord re-establish the modern communication network. Technical support from Sessionite clerics is indispensable for portable terminals (handyterms), drones, and even the master control system of Dijiang.

The second is the Resurgonites. Outsiders may regard this branch as the military arm of the Cabal of Tranquility as it is full of clerics clad in heavy armor and wielding heavy guns and cannons. The Resurgonites are charged with the defense of Cabal temples. They also actively take part in the excavation of Precursor ruins. Although they claim their goal is to "restore the Holy City", not every action is an act of faith. Some simply enjoy this way of life.

The third faction is the Veritarites, whose clerics place faith above all else. By the time these clerics first journeyed to Talos-II, the great upheaval of the Holy City had already transformed the Lateran faith itself. The Veritarites are committed to healing the long-term psychological trauma suffered by the Civilization Band following the collapse of the Cosmic Gate. Through spiritual guidance and public charity campaigns, they seek to restore human connections and compose a new chapter in theological philosophy on Talos-II.

findings.name: Civilization Band
findings.text:
The Civilization Band designates the collective human societies operating under the framework of the Band Accord (hereinafter referred to as the Accord), adhering to its established statutes and regulations.

The Civilization Band comprises various sized factions, coalitions, and organizations. Bound by Accord restrictions, it does not accept self-declared "nation-states" as members. Using the Accord as its foundational framework, it promotes technical specialization and autonomy among members, sustains humanity's basic survival on Talos-II, and strives for human self-actualization on this world. Individuals possessing Civilization Band recognized status who reside within territories administered by its constituent factions and organizations are designated "Band Residents". This group constitutes over 90% of Talos-II's total population.

The three largest factions within the Civilization Band are the United Workers' Syndicates of Talos II (known as the UWST), the Talos-II General Chamber of Commerce (known as the TGCC), and the Affiliated Hongshan Academy of Sciences of Tianshi Bureau of Great Yan (known as the HAS). Under the Accord's framework, these three entities collectively hold the designation of "Unshakable Members of the Band Accord" (abbreviated as U3). They are widely recognized as the "Major Three" or the "Big Three".

Endfield Industries also stands as a significant member of the Civilization Band. For convenience and to maintain neutrality, Dijiang houses dedicated conference facilities where Band members conduct general discussions regarding Accord amendments and other collective matters.

findings.name: Cosmic Gate
findings.text:
Cosmic Gates represent a classification of precursor transportation infrastructure whose operational principles remain only partially understood by contemporary science. On Terra, these structures were positioned at both the northern and southern extremities of the planet's major continents. Talos-II, by contrast, possesses only one confirmed Cosmic Gate, located at its northern polar region.

When discovered by humanity, both Cosmic Gates on Terra were found in states of severe damage. Through immense effort, researchers managed to restore the less-damaged northern structure, commonly called the "Sami Cosmic Gate". Exploration revealed it led to what was initially termed "subspace," though this has since been determined not to be a true Ætherside. After countless attempts and sacrifices, following the reactivation of the precursor celestial calculation and measurement device known as the "Celestial Fulcrum" within Terra's home star system, humanity finally identified the Cosmic Gate's paired counterpart. This breakthrough allowed the first steps onto the soil of Talos-II.

During the colonization of Talos-II, humanity exercised deliberate caution by refraining from any modifications to the planet's Cosmic Gate. This prudent approach meant no additional Cosmic Gates were discovered in the process. However, scientists across the Civilization Band widely maintain that other Cosmic Gates must exist within Talos-II's star system.

This vital passage between Terra and Talos-II remained operational for five years until the outbreak of the First Aggeloi War, when humanity lost access to the Talos-II Cosmic Gate. Today, the Talos-II Cosmic Gate lies shrouded beneath the Aurora of Talos-II, beyond the reach of human activity. Its current condition, along with the status of Terra on the other side, has become inaccessible to human knowledge.

findings.name: Cradle of the Ages
findings.text:
The Cradle of the Ages is an extraordinary Originium marvel located deep within the Origin Lodespring region.

During Valley IV's initial development phase, severe energy shortages threatened the colonization effort. The Endministrator addressed this by planting the Great Originium Oak, a creation of the Originium Arts, in the Origin Lodespring region. People harvested branches and foliage from this arboreal marvel to establish the territory's first power plant and quarry, initiating a positive cycle for expansion. Approximately two decades ago, when the Giant Aggelos "Astarron" assaulted the valley and all countermeasures failed, the UWST made the fateful decision to detonate the Great Originium Oak. The catastrophic energy release obliterated "Astarron".

Though only the root system remains of the Great Originium Oak today, stripped of its ability to rapidly generate Originium clusters, workers still honor this former guardian. They refer to the relic as the "Cradle of the Ages", expressing gratitude for how it nurtured multiple generations in Valley IV.
findings.unlock: Complete the main mission Chapter I Process III: Shattered Veins

findings.name: Denstacks
findings.text:
Denstacks serve as the signature battlefield installation of the Bonekrusher Clan.

During the era when the Landbreakers remained united, the warlord Jakub ruled over them. This former hero who had turned his back on the Civilization Band brought forth a witchcraft device known as the Denstack from Seš'qa. The Denstack absorbs Blight and disperses them in mist form.

When Denstacks are erected and their haze begins to spread, all Originium-based devices within range experience significant disruption. This includes but is not limited to drones, communication systems, and transport vehicles. Following the Landbreakers' fragmentation, the most violent remnant faction, the Bonekrusher Clan, inherited these devices. They deploy them as strategic installations to conceal raids and plundering operations. The appearance of multiple Denstacks often signals the clan's preparation for large-scale assaults on surrounding areas.

Following Nefarith's modifications, the contemporary Denstack now enhances the combat capabilities of Bonekrushers operating within its influence zone. However, when ordinary individuals inhale its haze, they experience significant physical discomfort beginning from the respiratory tract, with some developing auditory and visual hallucinations.
findings.unlock: Progress through the main mission Chapter I Process I: Secure Sanctuary

findings.name: Dijiang
findings.text:
OMV Dijiang is a spacecraft in geostationary orbit above Talos-II. It is the current headquarters of Endfield Industries.

Humanity lost its lifeline to Terra when the Cosmic Gate collapsed and the First Aggeloi War broke out. In the moment of despair against this sudden threat, human factions that included the UWST, HAS, and TGCC jointly initiated several research projects. OMV Dijiang was one of them.

After a series of events, Endfield Industries became part of humanity's war effort. Many rare and non-renewable tech resources were used to construct Dijiang in Talosian orbit. This was a feat of technological marvel that could never be replicated.

Dijiang is powered by a massive core of Protocol-Originium. The core is responsible for keeping the Master Protocol System operational and supporting various subsystems that include the Tele-Protocol (TP) and Automated Industry Complex (AIC).

findings.name: Endfield Industries
findings.text:
Endfield Industries is an independent company that primarily focuses on providing pioneering industrial technologies and services. The Endfield vision is to build and expand into the frontiers of the Talos-II.

When the first scientific survey teams arrived at Talos-II, Rhodes Island and its other partners jointly founded Endfield Industries to serve as a think tank and forward prospector. The Endministrator led numerous Endfield geological survey teams and generated detailed maps for numerous frontier regions. After the link between Talos-II and Terra was severed, the frontiersmates of the new world were forced to face the threats posed by the Aggeloi and the Blight on their own. Endfield thus stepped to the forefront, and continued to do so till this very day.

Endfield became an integral part of the future of Talos-II due to its novel technologies such as Protocol-Originium teleportation, Automated Industry Complex (AIC), controlled Originium distribution, and OMV Dijiang (the only orbital vehicle of Talos-II). As dangers emerged to threaten the budding civilization of the new world, Endfield once again initiated its journey to expand the frontiers.

findings.name: Feranmut
findings.text:
Feranmuts are gargantuan creatures indigenous to the planet Terra.

Known Feranmuts measure anywhere from several hundred to several hundred thousand meters in size. Their presence alone could alter natural laws, transform planetary environments, and even give birth to new forms of life. Additionally, every known Feranmut wields unique powers that far surpass modern bases of Originium Arts Theory. One of the most commonly known Feranmut powers is the ability to create proxies". These "proxies", while serving as a manifestation of Feranmut power, resemble Terran humans and serve as a channel by which Feranmuts communicate with Terran Civilization. In fact, many proxies" have traveled across the Land for centuries without any humans detecting their true nature

The Terran nation of Yan, from which Hongshan Academy of Sciences (HAS) hails, has performed the most extensive "Feranmut" studies and even fought a war against Feranmuts in its history. To this day, HAS remains the "expert regarding Feranmuts" in the Civilization Band. Armed with its strength in Feranmut studies, HAS maintains a cautious yet stable relationship with the Feranmut Proxy while it channels Feranmut powers into technological research and development. The novel Originium material known as "Xiranite" is a key result of this effort.
findings.unlock: Progress through the side mission A Dreamscape Shattered by Her Arrow

findings.name: Feranmut Sui
findings.text:
The Feranmut Sui (or simply as "Sui") is the last Feranmut to be defeated and sealed during the "Great Hunt" of Yan.

In the legends of Yan, a True Lung once mobilized the powers of an entire nation and personally led talented scholars and powerful warriors in the "Great Hunt" that decimated the once godlike Feranmuts. During this war, a powerful Feranmut named Sui betrayed its own kin and assisted the Yanese nation in this war of subjugation. After paying a steep price, the Yanese people finally defeated all Feranmuts, including Sui itself, and achieved the great feat known as the "Ennoblement of the Gods". This event also marked the turning point at which the fate of the Yanese nation was returned to the hands of the mortals.

Meanwhile, we also know clearly that the "Great Hunt" that actually took place in history may differ from the details embellished by the myths. However, all matters associated with Sui are treated as top secrets of the Yanese state. Many researchers have spent entire lifetimes in pursuit of the truth but never came close. Nevertheless, information provided by the Hongshan Academy of Sciences (HAS) and the archives of Rhodes Island indicates that the twelve proxies of Sui once walked upon the Land of Terra.

As of today, HAS remains extremely prudent on issues related to Feranmuts, though it has also achieved a close partnership with the thirteenth proxy of Sui. Both have worked together to improve crucial devices known as the Feranmut Hearts. Such devices are considered among the pinnacle of technological applications stemming from the HAS discipline of Feranmut studies, the technical origins of which can be traced back to the Age of Terra. Deep integration with Protocol-Originium technology eventually led to the current iteration. The interiors of the Marker Stone are furnished with multiple Feranmut Hearts working together, forming the foundation of the installation seen today.
findings.unlock: Progress through the main mission Chapter II Process IV: Phantom Wisps

findings.name: Hannabit Circuit
findings.text:
The Hannabit Circuit is a general term for certain groups of traveling wanderers who roam the wilderness of Talos-ll while sharing a distinct cultural identity.

Members of the Hannabit Circuit refer to themselves as "Songseekers" and see themselves as travelers, wandering scholars, and nomads. Songseekers roam the wildlands beyond the cities of the Civilization Band. They have mastered unique wilderness survival skills and crafting techniques, and have founded many self-sufficient pastoral tribes. Although different Hannabit tribes uphold radically different traditions, every Songseeker in the Circuit follows the same basic tenet - take up the wanderer's path to hone oneself, and seek a way to coexist with Talos-II.

The "Aldertones" of the Hannabit Circuit serve as guides and teachers. Each Aldertone has their own following, offering knowledge to their "Echolings" while wandering the world to validate and perfect their beliefs. The "Echolings" are apprentices and followers who acquire wisdom from their Aldertones and join them on their wandering journeys. A well-learned Echoling often gains enough experience to journey alone. When such Echolings gather their own following, they become Aldertones themselves - which is why the Hannabit Circuit is colloquially known as the "academy of the wilderness."

findings.name: Hongshan Academy of Sciences (HAS)
findings.text:
The Hongshan Academy of Sciences (HAS) is the largest and most professional integrated R&D institution of Talos-II. While the HAS continues to feed almost the entirety of the Civilization Band and enrich the bread baskets of the planet, it also made rapid and tremendous progress in various fields of emerging sciences.

The foundation of the HAS was laid down by a surveillance team from Yan dispatched to Talos-II. During the few short hours after the First Aggeloi War broke out, these Tianshis had the chance to return to Terra via the Cosmic Gate but they chose to stay and join the battle. This decision resulted in them and their descendants being stranded on Talos-II with other scientific surveyors and pioneers. Since these Tianshis treated themselves as representatives of the Tianshi Bureau, the Hongshan Crater discovered afterwards was bequeathed to these Tianshis to serve as the site of their new bureau. Since the Crater was extremely habitable, large scientific complexes and hydroponic facilities were built in this area. The region formally registered as the Hongshan Academy of Sciences days before the signing of the Band Accord.

To date, the HAS continues to call itself an R&D institution of Yan and govern its territories as such. It has established specialized ministries for raising livestock and crops. Occasionally, the HAS would receive criticism for its extremely strict standards of admissions and chronic shortage of Tianshis. However, the HAS always responded by emphasizing its compliance with the provisions of the Band Accord. Given such commitment to the quality, professionalism, and skills of its graduates, the most people of Talos-II have great respect for HAS scientists.

findings.name: Hub Base
findings.text:
The Hub Base serves as a crucial facility for Endfield Industries, dedicated to Automated Industry Complex research and Automated Industry Equipment manufacture.

Approximately two decades ago, the UWST eliminated the Giant Aggelos "Astarron" that assaulted Valley IV, though at grievous cost. The conflict left regional development paralyzed, creating an urgent need for economic revitalization. This timing coincided with Endfield Industries seeking a location with strategic accessibility and open terrain suitable for Automated Industry Complex development. The mutual needs led to a natural partnership, resulting in a renewable ten-year lease agreement. Construction of the Hub Base commenced shortly thereafter.

The Hub Base carries the critical mission of advancing Automated Industry Complex development. Since its establishment, it has efficiently completed research and implementation of numerous projects including industrial equipment miniaturization, flexible device deployment, and protocol control systems. While Endfield Industries maintains similar facilities across Talos-II, any quantified assessment of the company's technological progress over the past two decades would undoubtedly rank the Hub Base as its foremost contributor.

findings.name: Landbreaker
findings.text:
Landbreakers usually refer to groups of armed raiders in the fringes of society who make a living by robbery or other forms of criminal violence.

The concept of Landbreaking is unique to Talos-II. The origins of the Landbreakers can be traced back to the 90th year after the Terrans first arrived at Talos-II. Jakub Meissen, the Warlord of the Wilds, named his massive bandit army the "Landbreakers". The former hero of the Aggeloi War occupied a large Originium cultivation site and founded the most dangerous raider organization in the history of Talos-II. As a warlord, Jakub left a rather permanent mark upon Talosian history. Though he and his Landbreakers were completely defeated by the Civilization Band, people still use the term to describe organized groups of armed criminals that disregard the laws and order of civilization.

When Jakub Meissen's criminal organization was destroyed by the Civilization Band, his legacy was inherited by three major clans, namely the Bonekrushers, the Pack, and the Sandreavers. These clans have different perspectives on their relationship with the Civilization Band. In addition to the three major clans, numerous smaller Landbreaker clans and warbands are also active throughout Talos-II.

findings.name: Marker Stone
findings.text:
The Marker Stone is the first operational Tianshi Pillar to be formally deployed by the Hongshan Academy of Sciences (HAS).

The Tianshi built the Marker Stone to perform more than just Tianshi Pillar functions. The Marker Stone and its affiliated production facilities also supply Wuling with Xiranite. In other words, if anything were to happen to the Marker Stone, the entire city would be in grave danger. The Marker Stone area is also where the Wuling City Feranmut Heart is located. Joining two pieces of Xirancore Jade (the key source of power for the Feranmut Heart) in a precise fashion will start up the Feranmut Heart.

The Marker Stone and Wuling City share similar origins in that both were established in this stretch of previously unclaimed wilderness. To commemorate this crucial period in the history of the Wuling Scientific Developmental District, an Urban Development Hall was built in the Marker Stone area. The exterior walls of the hall also display important milestones dating from after the city's founding.
findings.unlock: Complete the main mission Chapter II Process IV: A Lethal Invitation

findings.name: North Wuling Exclusion Zone
findings.text:
The North Wuling Exclusion Zone (North Wuling EZ) is located at what was once the Wuling Science Station. Ten years ago, a small town was built around the Science Station. The town had amenities that included a school, a hospital, and Tanjian Hall. The latter trained many members of the Yinglung Special Task Force (YSTF), and even provided basic education for children of schooling age who lived together with parents working at the Science Station.

During Talosian Calendar Year 142, the Tianshi stationed at Wuling Science Station of the Hongshan Academy of Sciences (HAS) attempted to reverse the growth of the Very Large Rift (VLR) with Xiranite. This experiment triggered a rift rupture of disastrous effects, with Wuling Science Station and its prototype Xiranite facilities being completely engulfed by the Blight Tide within two hours. Although the HAS directed vast amounts of resources and personnel to support subsequent search-and-rescue operations, only a handful of survivors were saved. The HAS then committed all of its emergency response forces to contain the disaster within Yinglung Pass and enforced strict access control to the stricken area that covered the entirety of Wuling Science Station. This area became known as the North Wuling EZ.

For ten years, the HAS imposed a complete lockdown of the North Wuling EZ out of safety considerations for the Civilization Band, and even assigned Yinglung Special Task Force (YSTF) teams to long-term garrison duties at Yinglung Pass. After the completion of Wuling City, the HAS constructed a new comprehensive system for containing anomalous Blight phenomena in the North Wuling EZ. The system featured facilities based on Xiranite technology, such as the Tianshi Pillar Array.

During the early phases of North Wuling EZ lockdown, many within the Civilization Band questioned whether the HAS might abandon the region of Wuling entirely. Certain voices in the HAS seemed partial to this course of action, but the people of Wuling still hoped for a day when they would triumph over the VLR. The Wulingers remain strongly and wholly committed to this belief.
findings.unlock: Progress through the main mission Chapter II Process VII: Thus Begins the Homeward March

findings.name: Order of Steel Oath
findings.text:
The Order of the Steel Oath is a defensive force currently garrisoned in the high latitudes of Talos-II, far north of the Civilization Band.

As the shield of the Civilization Band, the Order of Steel Oath oversees territories that include the Polar Circle defense works, which it has been building for more than a century without pause, as well as fortress cities that house numerous non-combatants (including volunteers as well as family members of the Oathkeepers). The Order is a proud military organization, sustained by personnel, technology, and hardware supplied by the entirety of the Civilization Band. Its duty (also known as the "Steel Oath") is to hold the defense line along the Polar Circle of Talos-II against the Ankhors and the Aggeloi, and to do whatever is necessary to prevent a disaster like the First Aggeloi War from happening again.

During the First Aggeloi War, a motley force of soldiers from the various nations of Terra rallied and raised their battle colors on the polar fringes of Talos-II and became the predecessors of the Order. Together with the people of Samivegr, they dug a network of trenches beneath the Aurora and forged an indestructible alliance. Within the string of fortresses behind the Order's Polar Circle defenses, the Arsenals of Fort Forgefane churn out steel and artillery, while war relics that can be traced back to the Crystal Age of Terra are kept within the Order's vaults. Oathkeepers, whether they are fortress-born or hailing from the Civilization Band, are organized into banners. The blood-soaked pennants carried by banner ensigns are symbols of the Oathkeepers' indomitable will in battle.

findings.name: Originium
findings.text:
Originium is an energy-rich crystalline mineral. It was first brought to Talos-II by the arriving Terrans.

Originium exists in multiple distinct forms, serving as humanity's most vital natural energy source and industrial material. With its exceptionally high energy density, it can be directly combusted to release power for immediate use or undergo various refinement processes for specialized applications.

When Originium expends its vast internal energy, it leaves no residue like ordinary combustibles. Instead, it gradually breaks down into fine particulate dust, a transformation known as "Originium Activation." Though this activated state carries the risk of spreading Oripathy, such dangers have been effectively contained within Talos-II's controlled environments.

The energy released by Originium can be converted through multiple pathways into thermal energy and every other known form of power. This unique property, known as "Originium Adaptability," has cemented its irreplaceable role within human economic systems.

One of Terra's three "First Originium" fragments was transported to Talos-II, becoming the progenitor of all Originium on this world. This proliferation is made possible by the mineral's natural growth properties. A key mission of the United Workers' Syndicates of Talos II involves cultivating Originium clusters across the surface of Talos-II to ensure the sustainable harvesting of this vital resource.

A relatively recent discovery revealed that Originium was artificially created as an information carrier. It possesses the capacity to reshape its surrounding environment and even influence the course of biological evolution. The true intentions of Originium's creators toward Terran Civilization remain unclear. What can be stated with certainty is that separating humanity from Originium has become, by every measure, an impossibility.

findings.name: Originium Arts
findings.text:
Originium Arts represent humanity's methodology for channeling the energy within Originium through specific techniques, directing it into defined forms to achieve particular purposes.

During the dawn of Terran civilization, humans discovered their profound connection with Originium. They learned that in Originium-rich environments, they could manifest various natural phenomena through sheer will: flames springing from palms, frost forming from breath, lightning answering their gaze... These primal techniques became the first Originium Arts. As civilization advanced, people developed specialized methods to process Originium for enhanced Originium Arts. The devices created through these techniques became known as "Arts Unit". Those who primarily rely on such instruments to practice Originium Arts earned the designation of "Casters".

Later discoveries revealed that every individual possesses an innate affinity for specific types of Originium Arts and their mastery levels, a phenomenon termed "Originium Art Uniqueness". This inherent nature demonstrates that human capacity for channeling these arts varies fundamentally from birth. To bridge these natural disparities and harness the benefits of Originium Arts more efficiently, humanity developed technology to encapsulate these arts within crystalline units, releasing them through mechanical systems. These innovations, known as "Encapsulated Casting Units", transformed Originium Arts into standardized technology and paved the way for the explosive growth of Originium industry. On Talos-II, humanity continues to reap the conveniences born from this revolutionary development.

findings.name: Originium in Talos-II
findings.text:
In Talos-II, Originium remains the primary source of energy and a key material for industrial production and the Arts.

The hostile environments of Talos-II motivated scientists to achieve numerous theoretical breakthroughs. The last 150 years witnessed the release of new power generation and industrial production solutions of ever increasing efficiency. However, Originium remains the basis for all these advancements. The frontiersmates of the new world know very well that the most basic forms of industrial production could not be achieved without Originium boilers or Originium Arts.

The frontiersmates also chose to learn from the mistakes of the past and look for new solutions. The development of the Controlled Originium Distribution (CORD) technology gave a degree of control over the growth of Originium clusters and made it possible to "cultivate" them in Oripathy specific areas. CORD greatly reduced the likelihood of Catastrophes in Talos-II. Additionally, Long-term Oripathy Treatment (LORIT) was well-received by the Talosians. Preventive Oripathy Shots (PORIPS) and therapeutic suppressants were also developed. The Infected were no longer stigmatized in Talosian towns and villages now that treatment became readily available. Though the situation looks hopeful, Originium-related issues and challenges continued to affect the new world.

findings.name: Protocol-Originium
findings.text:
Protocol-Originium (Protorig) is one of the core technological marvels achieved by Endfield Industries. A network of Protorig crystals was used to establish a tele-protocol network. Transferring personnel and materials between two locations across great distances is no longer science fiction nor dependent on legacy tech such as the Cosmic Gate.

Shortly after arriving at Talos-II, many scientific research teams noticed the interactions between Originium and Æther energy and how the said interactions affected physical phenomenon and spatial continuity. Led by the Endministrator, Endfield carried out extensive research on this phenomenon, created the special Protocol-Originium (Protorig), and identified a means of utilizing multiple Protorigs to create a tele-protocol (TP) network.

However, the TP technology received little attention when first released as its Protorig system uses the extremely hazardous Æther and a single trip can only move a very limited number of personnel and resources. The breaking out of the First Aggeloi War changed everything. The use of both the Protorig and the TP network was validated in the brutal fields of battle and secured humanity's survival.

findings.name: Qingbo Hero
findings.text:
Qingbo Hero (or "Qingbo Haojie" in Yanese) is a common vernacular phrase used by the residents of Qingbo Stockade. The term often refers to pugilists who pursue fighting prowess, uphold a code of honor, and continue the practice of martial traditions.

According to oral accounts given by Stockade residents, their ancestors had lived through the chaos of war. These experiences taught everyone in the Stockade to exercise constant vigilance and preparedness against any potential threat or disaster. When the Stockade was first built, the practice of traditional Yanese martial arts was already part of Stockade culture. Almost all Stockaders, regardless of age or skill, trained in Yanese combat techniques to strengthen their physique and to defend their homes. Those with exceptional talent might also leave the Stockade to roam the lands with the aim of further elevating their fighting abilities.

Ten years ago, numerous Qingbo Stockaders with combat training were involved in a violent confrontation with Wuling City that resulted in casualties for both sides. Since the incident, many Stockaders skilled in fighting either left their homes or retreated into an ennui of defeat. The martial traditions of Qingbo Stockade gradually died out, and the battle arena that the Stockaders once used to identify their best heroes has remained silent until this day.
findings.unlock: Complete the Narrative Event: A Fistful of Reflections

findings.name: Qingbo Stockade
findings.text:
Qingbo Stockade is a small riverside community located in the outskirts of Wuling City. The Stockaders were already living in this part of Wuling before the scientific survey team from Hongshan Academy of Sciences arrived in this region.

The stacked multistory design, hanging architecture, and simple waterworks are capable of supporting those living in Qingbo Stockade. Although Stockaders often steal and raid supplies from Wuling, the community is largely self-sufficient.

After analyzing field investigations and testimonies from actual Stockaders, folk historians believe that the founding of Qingbo Stockade occurred during the Humiliation War. That shameful conflict made many lose hope in the future of the Civilization Band. Such sentiments must have affected the Stockade founders as well. They ventured to the region of Wuling, found a new home on this alien planet, and expanded it into the Qingbo Stockade we see today.

Oral testimonies from multiple elderly Stockaders describe how their ancestors used their skills and techniques to discover a pristine sanctuary amidst the Blight-flooded landscape of Wuling. The earliest Stockaders lived around the Ancestral Spring and devised simple, direct solutions to survive the unforgiving environment of Talos-II. To the Qingbo Stockaders, the Blight Tide was a disaster but also kept them free from outsiders until the arrival of the Tianshi from Hongshan.
findings.unlock: Progress through the main mission Chapter II Process III

findings.name: Race
findings.text:
Race refers to groups of humans distinguished by shared physical characteristics and/or cultural traditions.

According to Terran tradition, humanity on Talos-II is classified into three major racial categories: the Elders, the Ancients, and the Sarkaz.

The Elders and Ancients constitute the majority of Talos-II's population. The division between these two categories originated from early Terran social dynamics described as "nurturance and protection" versus "subjugation and dominion". These distinctions were based on social relationships rather than physical characteristics. When classified by physical traits and cultural traditions, typical Elders include Draco, Hippogryph, Lung, and Kylin, who represent a smaller portion of the population. Notable Ancients comprise Feline, Liberi, Cautus, and Forte, encompassing the vast majority of human individuals.

Conventionally, the term "Sarkaz" refers to the majority of this racial category, with few exceptions such as Sankta and Durin. Unlike the Elders and Ancients, they trace their ancestry to a distinct lineage. After the Ancients, the Sarkaz form the second largest demographic on Talos-II. Throughout Terran history, the Sarkaz engaged in significant racial conflicts with both Elder and Ancients. On Talos-II, these historical hostilities have largely been resolved. However, the Sarkaz now face a series of unforeseen challenges on this new frontier. Currently, Seš'qa serves as the primary representative of Sarkaz cultural traditions within the Civilization Band.

The following is a list of common racial descriptions used by the Terrans:

1. Ancients

Archosaurian: A race whose members usually have bulky tails. Archosaurians are proud of their culture and prefer living in rainforests. Adapting to the climate of Talos-II has been quite a challenge to them.

Ægir: A race with close affinity to water. Their ancestors built an entire nation under the sea, complete with undersea metropolises. They also played an important role in the history of Terra.

Aslan: A subgroup of the Felines that diverged because of their unique culture and traditions. Characterized by their golden hair and tails, Aslans could also claim descent from a royal family that ruled some Terran nation. However, the modern Aslans have already come to terms with this fact — There are no kings or queens in Talos-II.

Caprinae: A race with great love of their horns. Terrans stereotypically view Caprinae as expert casters of the Originium Arts. After all, the legendary "Witch King" was a Caprinae.

Cautus: A race characterized by their long ears and short, fluffy tails. Cautuses prefer living in Cautus communities and place great importance in familial ties. These are Terran traditions that they kept alive.

Elafia: A race sporting branching antlers atop their head. Their ancestors mostly lived in Terran countries with plenty of forested regions.

Feline: One of the most common races. Most Felines have pointed ears, long tails, and keen senses. They are widely distributed across the entire Civilization Band.

Forte: A race that usually sports horns, powerful physique, and excellent endurance. Fortes proved to be indispensable for the exploration and development of Talos-II.

Kuranta: A race with exceptional endurance and skills in running and jumping. The Kuranta were the ones who established the knightly and chivalric traditions.

Liberi: A populous race characterized by feathers and lighter builds. They are one of the most common races in both Terra and Talos-II.

Lupo: A subgroup that diverged from the Perros. The famous Landbreaker Clan known as the Pack have many Lupo members.

Perro: A race with puffy, furry tails. They usually live in large families and place great emphasis in keeping peace and harmony with each other. Perros are also one of the most common races of Talos-II.

Phidia: A race with tall, slender builds, long tails, and pointed ears. Some may also have scales growing on their bodies. Phidians were already quite rare in Terra, and became only rarer in Talos-II.

Savra: A scaled race known for their longevity. Like Phidians, many Savrans have long, scaly tails as well. Unlike the Phidians, their skins tend to be rougher and more resilient.

Ursus: A race characterized by their bulky stature, endurance, and cold resistance. The Ursi once established a nation of the same name in Terra, and are now active throughout Talos-II.

Vouivre: A horned race whose members commonly serve as mercenaries. Most Vouivres are valiant and capable of warriors. They are sometimes mistaken as Dracos.

Vulpo: A subgroup that diverged from Perros. Vulpos are known for their light, nimble builds.

Zalak: A race with light, nimble bodies and characterized by their ear tufts. Zalaks are already famous for their tenacity and ability to survive harsh environments in the Age of Terra.

Other Ancients: Anurans, Ceratoes, Itra, Manticores, Petrams, Pilosa, and Reprobas also crossed the Cosmic Gate and arrived at Talos-II. These races were already quite rare in Terra. Their rarity has not changed in Talos-II.

2. Elders

Draco: An Elder race with magnificent horns and majestic tails. Dracos are often mistaken as Vouivres due to their rarity.

Kylin: An old race that hailed from the Terran nation of Yan. The Kylin were the ones that created Lei Fa (thunder arts), a unique form of the Originium Arts still being used by the Tianshi from the Hongshan Academy of Sciences.

Lung: Widely held as the "oldest race of Terra", the Lung occupied prestigious roles in the Terran nation of Yan.

Other Elders: Established Terran traditions of racial classification regard many Ancient subgroups as Elders. Examples include the Hippogryph subgroup of Liberi, the Cerberus subgroup of Perros, and the Nine-tailed Vulpo subgroup of Vulpos.

3. Sarkaz

Sarkaz: The Sarkaz are the original natives of Terra and the only true "visitors" of Talos-II. Their incredibly complex history and relations with other races cannot be summarized in a few pages. However, most Sarkaz living on Talos-II have chosen to leave the past behind. While the Sarkaz can be further subdivided, most still prefer to call themselves 'Sarkaz' for convenience.

Anasa: An ancient Sarkaz leader migrated to the eastern lands of Terra and his Sarkaz followers adopted a new cultural identity known as the Anasa. They also created a unique and long-venerated philosophy that still exerts influence over people living on Talos-II.

Durin: A Sarkaz race characterized by their smaller statures. Generations of subterranean life caused the Durin to diverge from other Sarkaz. They are renowned for their technological expertise as well as appetites for drink and merrymaking. Life in Talos-II hardly changed these customs.

Sankta: A Sarkaz race whose cultural identity was changed by the Precursor's "Personality and Cognitive Synchronization" (PCS). The Sankta are often called "angels" as they are born with halo and wings. This name fell out of use for obvious reasons — However, most Sankta don't really mind.
